messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Re: poppr beginner
messages.body_plain:
Hello

I wonder how to see/ include the p-values of IA and rD in the analysis?
Many thanks,
Clement

On Thursday, January 8, 2015 at 1:00:38 PM UTC-8, KMTsui wrote:
> Thanks. Will follow.
>
> On Thursday, January 8, 2015 at 12:58:07 PM UTC-8, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
> > Yes, if your data is haploid, change the data set to haploid.
> >
> > Zhian
> >
> > > On Jan 8, 2015, at 12:56 , KMTsui <cleme...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > >
> > > Hello Zhian
> > >
> > > My original data set is haploid, but I changed it homozygous diploid in Genalex.
> > > When I change the ploidy =2,  this is the result:
> > > 2 alleles cannot be coded by a total of 1 characters
> > >
> > > How to get around with this? Shall I change the dataset to haploid.
> > >
> > > Thanks, KM
> > >
> > > On Thursday, January 8, 2015 at 11:22:06 AM UTC-8, Zhian Kamvar wrote:
> > > Hi KM,
> > >
> > > From the format of your file, the easiest way to read in your data would be to use the function read.csv to load the data into R and then the function df2genind (see section 4.2 of the adegenet basics tutorial) to convert it to a genind object.
> > >
> > > Note that for your data set, you have the sample names in column 1 and the population names in column 2, so you will need to use some subsetting (here's a tutorial).
> > >
> > > Here's some example code:
> > >
> > > snps.df <- read.csv("GC_snp_CADM.csv", head = FALSE, sep = ",")
> > > # note that I'm telling read.csv that the file has no column names with head = FALSE
> > >
> > > snps <- df2genind(snps.df[, -c(1, 2)], ind.names = snps.df[[1]], pop = snps.df[[2]],ploidy = 1)
> > > # Change the ploidy to whatever you need
> > >
> > > poppr(snps)
> > > # Calculate index of association and basic summary statistics
> > >
> > > Hope that helps,
> > > Zhian
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > On Thursday, January 8, 2015 at 10:17:55 AM UTC-8, KMTsui wrote:
> > >
> > > Hello
> > >
> > > I am a beginner in R and I want to calculate the index of association by poppr for each of the population within the SNPs dataset (attached). It is derived a csv sheet prepared for genalex.
> > >
> > > I installed the poppr package in R but could not load the file (e.g. LL_snp_CADM.csv) into the software. Do you have any suggestions on the input file format? or command line?
> > >  e.g. >- read.genalex or data()
> > >
> > >  If I cam able to load the file, then I can use the command ia .... (on manual p. 27) to calculate the index. Am I right? I will appreciate your comments.
> > >
> > > Many thanks,
> > > regards,
> > > KM
> > >

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] poppr beginner
messages.body_plain:
Change the "sample" flag: http://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/poppr/functions/ia

This works for the "poppr" and "ia" functions

Zhian
